blocks.text: Following the census and plague, David identifies a specific location as the site for the LORD's house and the altar for Israel, designating it as the center of national worship.

David undertakes extensive preparations for the temple construction. He gathers the resident aliens in the land as workers and organizes stonemasons to quarry and dress stone. He accumulates large quantities of iron for nails and door fixtures, bronze in abundance, and cedar wood supplied by merchants from Sidon and Tyre. Recognizing that Solomon, his young son, will undertake the actual construction and that the temple must be extraordinarily magnificent and renowned throughout all lands, David establishes a comprehensive foundation of materials, skilled personnel, and organizational structures to enable Solomon's work.

David formally calls Solomon and charges him to build the house of the LORD, God of Israel. David explains that although he himself desired to build God's house, the LORD instructed him that he could not—he had shed blood abundantly through his many wars. The LORD will instead raise up a son who will be a man of rest and peace, to whom God will give respite from all enemies. This son will build the house for God's name and be established in an eternal kingdom over Israel.

David concludes his charge with blessing and exhortation. He entrusts Solomon to God's presence and asks that God grant him success and discretion and understanding for the work. David also emphasizes that Solomon's prosperity will depend on faithfully observing the statutes and ordinances that God revealed to Moses, urging him to keep the law of the LORD throughout his reign.
